target.title: fix(web-media): add timeoutMs option to WebMediaOptions for remote fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared web-media loader only enforces a body-chunk idle guard (`readIdleTimeoutMs`). A remote endpoint that accepts the TCP connection but withholds response headers forever leaves the fetch pending indefinitely — `readIdleTimeoutMs` only governs gaps between body chunks, never the pre-header stall. The Tlon channel's two remote media paths (`extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.ts` download, `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts` URL-backed image upload) inherit this gap and currently have no caller-supplied deadline.

This PR fixes both at the root: it adds an optional total-request lifetime (`timeoutMs`) to the shared `WebMediaOptions` seam and forwards a 15-minute ceiling through both Tlon call sites.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Aligns to the **15-minute bounded-media ceiling** from canonical precedent #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`, `CAMERA_URL_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`).
- Owns the shared `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs` seam so the same total-request lifetime can be reused by other bounded fetchers (e.g. the agent-tools PR #103209).
- `readIdleTimeoutMs` (body-gap, 30 s) stays separate and tighter; slow-but-progressing transfers are still bounded by the body-idle guard while a never-responding endpoint is now aborted at the overall deadline.
- Tlon is the first consumer; the seam is exported so future callers can opt in without a second plumbing change.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — adds optional `timeoutMs?: number` to `WebMediaOptions` (after `readIdleTimeoutMs`) and forwards it through `loadWebMediaRaw` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer` → `fetchGuardedMediaResponse` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` (creates an `AbortController`, passes the signal via `init.signal`).
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.ts` — sets `timeoutMs: TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000` next to the existing `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts` — sets `timeoutMs: TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000` in the `readRemoteMediaBuffer` call for URL-backed image uploads.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts` — updated assertions to `expect.objectContaining({ ..., timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000 })` (exact `toHaveBeenCalledWith` would go stale when fields are added — see [[clawsweeper-proof-gate-bound-timeout-prs]]).
- `src/media/web-media.test.ts` — adds the shared-loader **real-HTTP-server proof** (below).

## User Impact

- Tlon media downloads and URL-backed image uploads against stalled endpoints now abort at 15 minutes instead of running indefinitely. Behavior on normal-speed transfers is unchanged because `readIdleTimeoutMs` still fires first for slow-but-progressing body chunks.
- Slow transfers that genuinely exceed 15 minutes will now fail intentionally — this is the documented bounded-media contract from canonical precedent #103266.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (shared-loader run)

Added in `src/media/web-media.test.ts > aborts a real stalled HTTP server via the overall timeoutMs deadline`. Unlike the previously existing mock-`fetchImpl` test (which is unit-level proof only), this one starts an actual Node.js `http.createServer` that accepts the connection but never calls `res.writeHead`/`res.end`, then calls `loadWebMediaRaw` against `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/photo.png` using the **default `fetch`** (no `fetchImpl` override) with `timeoutMs = 400ms` and `readIdleTimeoutMs = 30_000ms` — the same forwarding shape both Tlon call sites use. The test asserts:

1. The promise rejects (timeout fires).
2. Elapsed wall time is ≥ `timeoutMs - 50ms` (proves the wait happened) and < `timeoutMs + 5s` (proves it didn't fall back to the 15-min default).
3. The surfaced error has the exact shape the Tlon callers will propagate upstream: `MediaFetchError` with `code: "fetch_failed"`, `message: "Failed to fetch media from <url>: request timed out"`, and `cause: TimeoutError("request timed out")`.

Focused suite run (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts --reporter=verbose
…
 ✓ |media| src/media/web-media.test.ts > loadWebMedia > aborts a real stalled HTTP server via the overall timeoutMs deadline 423ms
 ✓ |media| src/media/web-media.test.ts > loadWebMedia > applies the shared remote read idle timeout for raw web media loads 22ms
…

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  77 passed (77)
```

Surfaced error captured from the test (this is what the Tlon callers will propagate):

```json
{
  "name": "MediaFetchError",
  "code": "fetch_failed",
  "message": "Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:PORT/photo.png: request timed out",
  "cause": {
    "name": "TimeoutError",
    "message": "request timed out"
  }
}
```

The 423ms elapsed time for the `400ms` `timeoutMs` test confirms the AbortSignal fires at the deadline through the full production path (`loadWebMediaRaw` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer` → `fetchGuardedMediaResponse` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `init.signal` → `globalThis.fetch`), not via a mocked rejection. Both Tlon call sites use the same `loadWebMediaRaw` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer` code path with `timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000`, so this shared-loader proof covers the timeout mechanism that both Tlon callers rely on.

### Canonical precedent

Merged #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`) established `15 * 60_000` as the bounded-media total-request lifetime for the "server never responds" stall class. This PR aligns both Tlon callers and the shared seam to the same ceiling.

### Tlon call-site coverage

Both Tlon files were updated with the new `timeoutMs` constant and both colocated test files were updated:

- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.ts` — `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`
- `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts` — `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts` — `expect.objectContaining({ timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000 })`
- `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts` — `expect.objectContaining({ timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000 })`

The `objectContaining` pattern (instead of exact `toHaveBeenCalledWith`) keeps the assertions robust against future field additions — the canonical precedent PR #103266 hit this exact issue with stale exact-match tests.

### Coordination with #103209

This PR owns the shared `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs` seam and the two Tlon call sites. PR #103209 (agent-tools) keeps the same seam in its diff because cross-repo fork PRs cannot stack on each other's fork branches — each must typecheck standalone. The intent is for this PR to land first, then #103209 reduces to the three agent-tool callers only. The seam itself is identical (optional `timeoutMs?: number` after `readIdleTimeoutMs`, forwarded through `readRemoteMediaBuffer`).
